sources.citation: Beaty de Farris, Kathryn (comp.), with Pablo García Sánchez, Rubén García Sánchez, Jesús Ojeda Sánchez, Augustín San Pablo García & Apolonio Santiago Jiménez. 2004 [2nd ed; 1st ed. 2002]. Diccionario básico del mixteco de Yosondúa, Oaxaca. Serie de vocabularios y diccionarios indígenas "Mariano Silva y Aceves" 46. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. xvi+175 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Appendix 'Gramática mixteca', §1 'La fonología' (printed pp. 139–144 = PDF pp. 156–161) covers word shape (CVCV couplet, long/broken/checked vowels), three level tones alto/medio/bajo (§1.2, pp. 140–141), tone combinations and letters. Nothing on word stress; 'acento' occurs only as 'acento agudo' = the high-tone diacritic (p. 140). Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page for yoso1239 (https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/yoso1239) and classification tree
sources.note: No descriptive content. Confirms yoso1239 has no dialects; sister languages in Chalcatongic (chal1278) are San Miguel El Grande Mixtec (sanm1295, mig; dialect 'San Miguel Chalcatongo' = sanm1296), Atatláhuca (mib), Santa Lucía Monteverde (mdv), Itundujia (mce), Sinicahua (xti), Tijaltepec (xtl). ELCat alt-name list lumps Chalcatongo/San Miguel el Grande under yoso1239, but Glottolog's tree does not. Only four descriptive refs (Farris 1992; Farris 2004; the 1992 volume; a duplicate).
No phonology content; cites Egland & Bartholomew 1983, Alexander 1980 (Gramática mixteca de Atatláhuca) and Macaulay 1996 (Chalcatongo) — both sister languages, not yoso1239.
